Not to be a downer nearly a year later, but the answer your question - no, I don't think there is anything to this picture. The reason? You said it yourself, you had HDR settings on.

High-dynamic-range imaging (HDRI or HDR) is a set of techniques used in imaging and photography to reproduce a greater dynamic range of luminosity than is possible with standard digital imaging or photographic techniques.

High-dynamic-range photographs are generally achieved by capturing multiple standard exposure images, often using exposure bracketing, and then later, merging them (usually within a photo manipulation program) into a single HDR image.

TL;DR your phone took a bunch of pictures with multiple exposure times and your phone pasted them into one image, that explains the weird black fire parts as well as the strange lighting conditions all over the photo.
